top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the original experiment that verified a sharp, falsifiable prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald flat bands at the magic angle) and opened a door to a gate-tunable platform for correlated and superconducting states, reproduced by many independent groups and carried into other moire systems. The Bistritzer-MacDonald-Jarillo-Herrero allocation maps onto the theory-plus-experiment chain, and a citation limited to flat bands and correlated phases avoids claiming the open pairing mechanism. Maturity (about eight years) and exposed credit (Cao, Dean, earlier theory) are real discounts, which is why optical lattice clocks (P001) is a close second as the most mature, cleanly attributed alternative; P003 is third because its allocation is unsettled, and no award is last.
